turns.prompt_text: I'm thinking what would be the best way to gather all of my statements. I know Rocket Money has to literally get access to everything, and I don't think I'm going to be able to set all of that up. But would I be able to route things from my bank statements and my credit cards to my email so that I can pull it from there? It doesn't need to be instantaneous. It just needs to be weekly or monthly.
turns.response_html:
It makes complete sense that you would want to avoid handing over the keys to all your financial accounts to a third-party app. Keeping your data in your own hands is a smart security practice, and you can definitely build a system that works for you directly through your inbox.

Here is the reality of how banks handle email: for security and privacy reasons, financial institutions will never attach your actual PDF statement or a raw data file directly to an email. Instead, they will send an email notification with a secure link to log in.

However, you can still build a highly effective, email-based system to track your finances. Here are the three best ways to set that up:

1. The Real-Time Ledger (Best for Searching)

Instead of waiting for a monthly statement, you can force your banks to treat your email inbox like a running ledger of your spending.

  • Set up Transaction Alerts: Log into your credit card portals (like your Amex, Citi, or FNBO accounts) and navigate to the Account Alerts or Notifications section.
  • Trigger on Every Purchase: Set up an email alert for "Any transaction greater than $0.00" or a very low threshold like $1.00.
  • The Result: Every time a subscription renews or a purchase is made, you get a clean text email with the merchant name, date, and amount. You can easily search your Gmail for these alerts later, giving you line-by-line visibility without needing a third-party app.

2. The Monthly Statement Funnel (Best for Archiving)

If you prefer to just sit down once a month and pull everything at once:

  • Enable Paperless Statements: Ensure all your accounts are set to "Paperless" or "Online Only" delivery.
  • Automate Your Inbox: Create a filter in Gmail to catch the exact sender addresses or subject lines (e.g., "Your statement is ready") and automatically route them to a specific label, such as "Statements to Download."
  • The Monthly Pull: Once a month, click through that label, log in via the provided links, and download your PDFs or CSV spreadsheets directly to your own secure folder.

3. Weekly Balance Updates

If you just want a routine pulse check without looking at line-by-line details, almost all issuers offer a weekly account summary email. You can opt into this feature to receive your current balance, recent payments, and available credit on a set day of the week, keeping you aware of your total spending trajectory without ever needing to log in.

turns.prompt_text: I think the best first step would be to just label exactly where everything is so that at the end of the month I can sit down and manually pull it. From there, I can figure out how to automate that. Because I already have everything going to Rocket Money, or at least a great amount of things going to Rocket Money, maybe I could just pull it all from there.
turns.response_html:
Using Rocket Money as your central hub is actually a very smart pivot. Since it is already aggregating your accounts, pulling from there will save you from having to log into a dozen different websites.

To get the best of both worlds, you can split your monthly routine into two parts: using Rocket Money for the raw data, and using Gmail to catch the official documents.

1. The Data Pull (Via Rocket Money)

Rocket Money is perfect for seeing all your line-by-line transactions across all your cards and bank accounts in one place.

  • Instead of manually copying data, you can log into the Rocket Money web dashboard (on your computer, rather than the phone app).
  • Navigate to your Transactions list and look for the Export to CSV option.
  • This gives you a clean spreadsheet of every purchase and subscription from the past month that you can drop straight into Excel, Google Sheets, or Obsidian to review your spending.

2. The Document Pull (Via Gmail Labels)

While Rocket Money is great for transaction data, it doesn't store your official PDF statements. It is still a great idea to build that Gmail label system as your "source of truth" archive.

Here is how to automate the labeling in Gmail so everything is waiting for you at the end of the month:

  1. Open Gmail and click the Show search options icon (the sliders) in the search bar.
  2. In the Includes the words field, type standard statement phrases like: "statement is ready" OR "statement available" OR "statement enclosed"
  3. In the From field, add the automated addresses of your specific banks. For example: americanexpress@welcome.americanexpress.com OR fnbo@notify.fnbo.com OR bestbuycard@info17.citi.com
  4. Click Create filter.
  5. Check the box for Apply the label, choose New label, and name it something like Financial/Monthly Statements.
  6. Click Create filter.

Now, whenever a month closes out, you can just click that label in your sidebar. All the links to download your official PDFs will be neatly grouped together, and you can pull your CSV from Rocket Money to review the actual numbers.
